# Accessibility

Build accessible interfaces using semantic HTML whenever possible.

## Images

- Meaningful images need useful alt text.
- Decorative images should use an empty alt attribute.
- Alt text should describe relevant content, not simply say "image" or "photo".

## Navigation

- All interactive functionality must be usable with a keyboard.
- Use semantic elements such as button, nav, main and footer.
- Do not use a div as a button when a native button is appropriate.
- Keyboard focus must remain visible.

## Content

- Use logical heading levels.
- Maintain sufficient text contrast.
- Do not communicate important information using color alone.

## Forms

When forms are introduced:

- Every input must have a clear label.
- Validation errors must be understandable in text.
- Required fields must be clearly identified.

## Responsive accessibility

Content should remain readable and usable on small screens and when text is enlarged.

Do not sacrifice accessibility for visual effects or animations.
